data.completion_memo: Capability warnings are now deduplicated per distinct warning per Chat, durably. RunEventStream::capability_warnings derives the active condition set from committed evidence (so a fresh stream per pass still sees prior warnings), commits each distinct warning once, and commits a workflow.capability-warning-cleared marker when a pass stops reporting it, so a later recurrence re-arms. The Chat timeline no longer projects workflow.capability-warning as a step, but the event remains committed and readable as Run evidence. A new Chat adapter (useCapabilityWarningNotices) publishes one standing status-bar notice per distinct warning with a condition lifetime, resolves on the cleared marker, and never reopens on hydration/replay. context_advisory_once is untouched. Verified: new Rust test (7 passes dedupe, second warning not suppressed, clear/re-arm, no conversation/context events) and new frontend tests (per-warning notice, no reload reopen); activityProjection test updated. Full desktop lib suite 572 passed (one pre-existing comfyui fallback-id failure); frontend 623 passed across 85 files; tsc clean. Committed 5a1be8c and pushed to main.

lines:
INTENT
A capability warning that says the same thing on every user message must stop being repeated Chat content. Today each distinct warning appears in the conversation as a timeline step, and it is re-emitted on every user message of the Chat, so the user reads the same list again and again. The user wants it as a status-bar notification instead, and only once for each individual warning.

EVIDENCE (recorded chat.07b0ca6e15e6824e2e5642e028395b3882fa3b0d)
- The user changed the workflow's MCP server settings during the Chat. The Chat kept working but now every new message produces the same list of errors.
- 6 distinct warnings, re-emitted on 7 requests: @22120, @22440, @24204, @24770, @25098, @25617, @26495 - 42 workflow.capability-warning events in total, all identical in text:
  "workflow binds MCP tool 'mcp://comfyui.bridge/<tool>', which this Chat never connected; start a New Chat to use it" for comfyui_get_workflow, comfyui_krea_2_turbo_text_to_image_upscaled, comfyui_list_node_types, comfyui_list_workflows, comfyui_run_workflow, comfyui_status.
- Those warnings were the only steady notification of a real condition: the Chat's frozen tool set is 49 tools with zero comfyui entries (context.delegation-scope @8), because a Chat keeps the authority it was frozen with. The condition is correct; repeating it in the conversation is not.
- The warning is not sent to the model: no workflow.capability-warning appears in any context.checkpoint selection of that chat. So removing it from the Chat timeline loses nothing the model reads, and the notification does not replace a model-visible fact.

WHERE THE REPETITION COMES FROM (verified)
- desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/service/current_configuration.rs (freeze_current_tools, ~line 95-123) re-derives the bound tool ids from the workflow document on every pass and returns the warning for each mcp:// binding not present in the frozen set. workflow_capabilities::warn already deduplicates identical strings within one document.
- desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/run_events.rs (capability_warnings, ~line 109-116) publishes one workflow.capability-warning per warning on every pass, so the dedup inside the document does not survive to the next user message.
- desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/service.rs (~1255) and graph_pass.rs (~435) carry the warnings for the pass.
- desktop/src/chat/activityProjection.ts:446 renders it as a Chat timeline step: kind "step", title "Unavailable capability", status "warning". That projection is what makes it conversation content.

REQUIRED CHANGE
1. Deduplicate by distinct warning per Chat, durably, not just within one document or one process. The existing per-stream helper RunEventStream::context_advisory_once (run_events.rs ~133-160) already implements "a persistent condition is worth saying once, not on every turn; a cleared condition re-arms" for compaction advisories, and is the intended pattern. Note its current shape keeps only the last body, so it is insufficient for 6 independent warnings: use one condition key per distinct warning (or a set), so warning 1 and warning 2 do not re-arm each other by alternating.
2. Re-arm honestly: if the condition clears and later returns, it notifies again. A cleared set must not permanently mute a real condition.
3. Stop rendering the warning as Chat timeline content. Remove the workflow.capability-warning branch in activityProjection.ts:446. Keep the event kind as the durable record - it remains the evidence for why a tool is unavailable and stays available in Run details' raw evidence and to context/compression logic.
4. Surface it as a status-bar notification through the existing shell-owned notification service (design element aworkit.desktop_ui.notifications: NotificationPort + DesktopStatusBar + docked details, publisher per feature, NotificationStore owns presentation dedup/ordering/expiry/ack - see docs/design-desktop-notifications-settings-return.md). Follow the existing Chat pattern (desktop/src/chat/useChatErrorNotices.ts): only newly committed events notify, hydration/replay never reopens an old warning, and one notification key per distinct warning message so the list shows each warning once.
5. Severity and lifetime: this is a standing condition of the Chat, not a failure, so "warning" severity with a condition lifetime keyed per warning (not a transient toast), unless the frontend pattern makes per-message condition keys unusable - in that case state the chosen lifetime in the task memo.
6. The user-visible text must still say what to do (the existing message already ends with "start a New Chat to use it"). Do not drop the actionable part when moving it to the status bar.
7. Do not change the authority rule that produces the warning. A running Chat keeps its frozen tool set; this task changes only where and how often the condition is reported.

ACCEPTANCE
- A test shows the same distinct warning is published once across many consecutive passes, and that a different warning is not suppressed by it (the alternating-warnings case).
- A test shows the warning is not projected as a Chat timeline item, while the workflow.capability-warning event is still committed and readable as evidence.
- A frontend test shows one status-bar notification per distinct warning, with no new notification when the Chat's event history is reloaded or replayed.
- The notification does not reach the model's context (no new selection content), matching the recorded chat where the warnings never entered the model's context.

DESIGN BOUNDARIES TO RECONCILE (do not drift)
- The compaction budget specification (aworkit.workflow_worker.context_compaction_budget) requires that a standing condition is published once per distinct body through the run event stream's context_advisory_once, and a cleared condition re-arms. This task extends that same mechanism to capability warnings, so the helper must keep that contract for both callers - do not weaken the advisory dedup to make the warning case easier.
- aworkit.desktop_ui.notifications owns the presentation contract: the store owns deduplication/ordering/expiry/acknowledgement and feature adapters own relevance. Publishing a capability condition is the feature adapter's job; the store must not learn about workflows.
- aworkit.desktop_ui.conversation currently owns the projection that renders the warning as a step. Removing that branch narrows its scope; the durable event and Run details evidence must stay intact.

data.title: Report each distinct capability warning once per Chat as a status-bar notification, not repeated Chat content
